title: M5CoreP4X UserDemo #1: IR 'Repeat x2' sends the NEC frame once (loop_count=1 normalized to no-loop)

firmware.build: not built; source-level comparison of the demo repository at cd1e1bd and HEAD 6b3c1c8
firmware.idf: ESP-IDF 6.1.0 (enforced by CMakeLists.txt:8,19-21); local tree fff9895c82d744c7237be8847347bdd1b07c6643

execution.environment: macOS arm64; read-only sparse clone of m5stack/M5CoreP4X-UserDemo; local ESP-IDF 6.1 source tree; local Device Service device list (read-only); hardware test center overview (read-only, no DUT used)

checks.detail: OPEN, author HalfSweet, English, 0 comments before this reply; no previous m5agent comment

ir_encoder.cpp:137-139 at HEAD and cd1e1bd sets loop_count = is_repeat ? 1 : 0 and returns rmt_transmit immediately; ui_function_irtxrx_window.cpp:556 is the only producer of is_repeat; :274 changes the label only
ESP-IDF 6.1 rmt_tx.c:550-551 maps loop_count == 1 to 0, so x2 and x1 submit the identical single transaction
CMakeLists.txt:8,19-21 aborts the build unless ESP-IDF is exactly 6.1, so the 6.1 semantics always apply
NEC frame is 34 symbols (nec_encoder.cpp:127-165); TX channel mem_block_symbols=64 becomes 2 blocks x 48 = 96 symbols (rmt_tx.c:131-136), below the loop-mode memory limit checked at rmt_tx.c:665-670
trans_queue_depth=2 (ir_tools.cpp:344) accepts a second queued transaction; rmt_tx_wait_all_done is only needed if the UI should report completion instead of queueing
RC5 branch never sets loop_count, so it is unaffected by the switch
the only ESP32-P4 test node is marked lent out / do not allocate; the fixture has no IR receiver or photodiode capture path
Device Service lists 36 profiles and no CoreP4X; the only P4 profile is Tab5 (ESP32-P4NRW32, esp-emulator-native), a different board with no CoreP4X model and no IR/RMT coverage
factory firmware IR waveform not captured; post-fix two-frame decode on a real NEC receiver not tested

limits: Source-level verification only; no hardware or virtual-device run
Does not measure frame gap, carrier duty or LED drive current
Does not prove a NEC receiver decodes two back-to-back frames after the fix
Design intent of 'Repeat' (two full frames vs NEC repeat code) still needs author confirmation
